transcript:
This is NPR News Now.
The latest headlines every hour.
- Live from NPR News in Washington, I'm Louise Schiavone.
As a new Democratic controlled Congress prepares
to convene within the next two months,
President Trump is bracing for investigations
with a new executive order directing federal contractors
who are asked to provide information
to consult with the White House
before talking to lawmakers.
NPR's Eric McDaniel has more.
- The White House can do anything they want
to try and prevent people from complying
with the legal investigatory powers of Congress.
But everyone, particularly if they're outside of government,
is taking individual legal risk
that the administration can't really insulate them from.
That's legal bills, that's time,
that's a potential contempt of Congress vote,
reputational cost, and all of this is pretty high stakes,
right, getting dragged before Congress is no small thing.
And remember what incoming House Oversight Committee
Chairman Robert Garcia, a Democrat, posted
when Democrats had won the majority.
He said lawyer up.
So his party and all of their investigatory committees
aren't gonna be timid at all
at pursuing their legal avenues.
- NPR's Eric McDaniel in Ukraine near Kiev,
a rescue operation is underway after a Russian attack
hit an apartment building killing at least three people,
injuring others and trapping several people in the rubble.
NPR's Eleanor Beardsley has the latest.
- Russia has intensified its drone and missile strikes
against Kiev and the surrounding region
as winter approaches.
In the last week, Kiev experienced
one of its heaviest assaults of the war
after Ukraine heavily damaged Putin's prized Kerch Bridge,
which links Russia with the occupied Crimean Peninsula.
Zelensky has repeatedly urged Ukraine's allies
to speed up promised air defense deliveries,
particularly interceptor missiles.
He says in the past week, Russia launched 2,700 drones,
1,460 glide bombs, and 165 missiles,
including upgraded North Korean ballistic missiles
at 20 Ukrainian regions.
President Trump said this week he believes Putin
is serious about ending the war.
Eleanor Beardsley in PR News, Lviv, Ukraine.
- Officials in the San Francisco Bay area
are preparing for Monster High King tides
after being hit with heavy rain last week.
Brian Kranz from member station KQED reports
the weather is being fueled by El Nino.
Some residents have already begun preparing for the worst.
In a muddy parking lot near the base shore,
Joseph Abu Halawa filled up large white plastic bags
with sand and loaded them into the back of his pickup.
- Definitely this year is probably the worst it's ever been.
- Recent historic rainfall flooded his house
in downtown Tiburon, and Abu Halawa isn't sure
the sandbags can hold off the king tides.
- I don't know, honestly.
I'm just doing it to make myself feel better
'cause the damage is already pretty bad, so,
but it's gonna make me feel at least more comfortable.
Like I'm doing something about the problem.
- The king tides are forecast to last three days,
peaking Wednesday at seven feet high.
For NPR News, I'm Brian Kranz.
- This is NPR.
After traveling for more than eight years,
a joint European Japanese mission has gone into orbit
around the planet Mercury.
The probe should provide scientists
with a wealth of new information
about the innermost planet in the solar system.
Joe Palka reports.
- Mercury is an intriguing planet.
It has an incredible number of scientific mysteries.
- Anne Pomier at the Carnegie Institution
is one of the scientists on the Bepi-Colombo mission.
She says scientists have found evidence
that there is ice at the poles of the planet,
odd for a planet so close to the sun.
It also has a larger metal core than expected.
- The fact that this planet is shrinking
also is another mystery.
- Bepi-Colombo is scheduled to start answering
scientific questions next spring,
but first it will spend several months
adjusting its orbit and checking out its instruments.
For NPR News, I'm Joe Palka.
- The Hunger Games movie franchise
powered into box offices this weekend
as Sunrise on the Reaping debuted
with an estimated $120 million in North American theaters.
This is twice as much as the previous installment,
the Ballad of Songbirds and Snakes.
Sunrise on the Reaping launched with $225 million globally,
this even as potential moviegoers were locked at home
playing Grand Theft Auto VI.
Pop star Miley Cyrus this weekend
married her boyfriend Lily Drummer Max Miranda
in Palm Springs, California.
Close family attended the nuptials
for the 33-year-old Cyrus and 28-year-old Miranda.
Photos from the event showed the two standing
by a swimming pool under a white floral arch.
I'm Louise Schiavone, NPR News, Washington.

topics.text: Trump executive order requires federal contractors to consult White House before talking to Congress
Russian attack on Kyiv apartment building kills at least three and traps people in rubble
Russia intensifies drone and missile strikes on Kyiv and surrounding region as winter nears
Bay Area officials prepare for king tides after heavy rain, with Tiburon resident sandbagging his house
Joint European-Japanese BepiColombo mission enters orbit around Mercury after eight-year journey
Sunrise on the Reaping opens to an estimated $120 million in North American box office
Miley Cyrus marries boyfriend Max Miranda in Palm Springs, California
